reasoning.overall: China PR have won only 2 of their last 4 matches and have been outshot on average (9.3 vs 11.6 shots) with just 2.3 shots on target per game, suggesting finishing inconsistencies despite playing at home in Beijing. Thailand arrive in strong form with 4 wins in their last 8, are unbeaten in their last 4 road/good-weather friendlies (2W 2D), and possess superior overall stats (56% possession vs 39%, 4.4 shots on target vs 2.3). Both teams scored in Thailand's last outing (2-2 vs Kuwait) and China just beat Singapore 2-1, indicating open attacking play. The match profile is normal-to-open with both sides capable of scoring. Key players include China's Yuning Zhang and Wenneng Xie for goals, and Thailand's veteran Teerasil Dangda and the active Jude Soonsup-Bell in attack. This is a competitive friendly where Thailand's better recent form and away robustness give them a slight edge, but China's home crowd and quality forward options make a home win entirely plausible.
reasoning.t1_result: Win probabilities reflect the competitive balance: China have home advantage and quality finishers, Thailand are in superior form with better possession metrics and shot accuracy. The draw probability is non-trivial given both teams' recent scoring patterns and the friendly nature of the fixture. China edge it slightly at home but away win is equally possible.
reasoning.t2_player: Both squads feature experienced internationals. China's attack led by Yuning Zhang, Wenneng Xie, and Lei Wu will look to exploit Thailand's occasionally high defensive line, while Thailand counter with Dangda's clinical finishing and the youthful energy of Soonsup-Bell on the wing. Midfield battles between Shangyuan Wang and Sarach Yooyen will be decisive.
reasoning.t3_events: Goals are likely from open play rather than set pieces given both teams' recent scoring patterns. Thailand scored first in 3 of their last 4 matches suggesting early away confidence. China will look to respond after going behind in their last two friendlies. Cards should be limited given the friendly context.
reasoning.t4_stats: Thailand dominate possession (56%) and shot metrics in recent games, while China have been efficient at home with 6 corners per game. The stats suggest Thailand control midfield but China create dangerous counter-attacks. Expect a competitive split in fouls and defensive actions.
